text:
alex: Hey @people-ops — quick Q: I start a 6-month assignment in Tokyo next month and my spouse will join on a dependent visa. Can I enroll them on Redwood's medical plan while I'm on assignment? Also need a carrier ID/plan code for a Japanese hospital registration.

nina (Benefits): Hi Alex — usually yes for short international assignments if you remain benefits-eligible. We need the dependent enrollment form + marriage certificate + copy of spouse passport/visa. Carrier rules vary for Japan; some hospitals ask for insurer phone + plan code. We can request a temporary insurer confirmation letter with the plan code.

alex: Awesome — any special steps for in-country providers? The local clinic said they bill insurers directly if we provide the "insurance number" and insurer phone.

ken: FYI, carriers often treat international outpatient claims as out-of-network. You can ask provider to bill, but many clinics expect patient-pay and then you submit for reimbursement. Keep itemized receipt with Japanese receipts (領収書) and any procedure codes.

benefits-bot: Automated: Dependent Enrollment Form -> https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/dependent-enroll. To request temporary insurer confirmation letter email benefits@redwood.com with subject "Insurer Letter - Alex [lastname] - Japan assignment". Typical turnaround 1-2 business days.

nina (Benefits): When you submit docs, include assignment dates and HR confirmation PDF. We will also request a digital ID card from the carrier; for international use they sometimes include an international billing code and phone number.

alex: Great — about receipts: clinic gave a handwritten receipt in yen. Is that ok or do I need a translation?

ken: Best to get an itemized receipt with clinic stamp. If handwritten only, scan and include a short English translation and a currency conversion screenshot (bank rate or xe.com) with the date of service. That speeds adjudication.

nina (Benefits): Also note: if the carrier denies direct billing, we can start a reimbursement claim once the dependent is enrolled (retro up to carrier policy). For urgent care you can request an expedited review; mark email subject "URGENT: Japan ER reimbursement".

alex: Thanks — I'll upload the marriage cert, passport pages, and assignment letter today. One last thing: will the digital ID card work for walk-in clinics or do I need the physical card?

benefits-bot: Digital ID cards are accepted for most providers. Some international clinics may still request a physical policy number or insurer phone; bring the benefits confirmation letter if you anticipate issues.

alex: Perfect, sending docs now. Appreciate the quick help.

nina (Benefits): Got it — will confirm next steps after we receive the email. :thumbsup:
